summary.text: The Counter-Reformation, also called the Catholic Revival or Catholic Reformation, was a period of Catholic resurgence in response to the Protestant Reformation.
It arose from the decrees of the Council of Trent (1545 to 1563) and produced anti-corruption efforts, internal reform, new religious orders and new art and musical styles.
Its reforms included seminaries to train priests, and it aimed to reach colonized lands and win back nations such as Sweden and England.

facts.label: Pope Paul III
facts.value: Considered the pope who began the Counter-Reformation

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: Translated from the German word Gegenreformation

facts.value: Seminaries were formed to train priests properly

facts.value: Reach colonized lands and reconvert Sweden and England

items.prompt: Massimo Firpo separates two ideas. One was founded on defending orthodoxy, repressing dissent and reasserting authority. Which?

options.label: Catholic Reformation, centered on the care of souls
The Radical Reformation, built on early practices
The Erasmian Reformation, shaped by scholars
Counter-Reformation, the specific one

items.explain: Firpo saw the Counter-Reformation as founded on defence of orthodoxy and repression of dissent, while the general Catholic Reformation centered on care of souls and renewal of the clergy.

items.prompt: A bishop in the 1560s opens a school for future priests. What is the point?

options.label: To train them in the spiritual life and Church traditions
To teach them Protestant doctrine so they can debate it
To turn parish priests into cloistered monks
To replace the Council of Trent's decrees

items.explain: Seminaries were formed for the proper training of priests in the spiritual life and the theological traditions of the Church.

items.prompt: Why did Catholic historians in 19th-century Germany dislike the term Counter-Reformation?

options.label: Catholic bishops had coined it to insult Protestants
It claimed the Church never needed reform before Luther
It implied only a reaction to Protestantism, ignoring reform within Catholicism
It left out the Council of Trent entirely

items.explain: Protestant historians used it as a negative, one-dimensional concept stressing reaction and resistance, which neglected reform within Catholicism, so Catholic historians shunned it.

items.prompt: In the 1500s new groups of clergy took special vows but were not bound to a monastery's daily prayer. What was their work?

options.label: Living cloistered and keeping the full daily prayers
Serving as the vicar of one parish
Teaching, preaching and hearing confession under a bishop
Governing the monasteries of older orders

items.explain: These regular clergy taught, preached and took confession under a bishop's direct authority, not linked to a specific parish like a vicar or canon.

items.prompt: The Council of Trent was asked to address corrupt bishops and the sale of indulgences. What did it do to the medieval church's core?

options.label: It upheld the basic structure, sacraments, orders and doctrine
It replaced bishops with elected councils
It abolished the sacraments the reformers rejected
It dissolved the religious orders

items.explain: The council tackled abuses but upheld the basic structure of the medieval church, its sacramental system, religious orders and doctrine.

items.prompt: Philip Neri's community, the Oratorians, wanted to draw ordinary people in. What did they use?

options.label: Public preaching alone from the pulpit
Hospital ministry to the sick
Long periods of cloistered silence
Music and singing

items.explain: The Oratorians used music and singing to attract the faithful.
